steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook udon in boiling water, stirring occasionally, until noodles are tender yet firm to the bite, 10 to 12 minutes. Drain.

Meanwhile, combine chicken broth, soy sauce, peanut butter, ginger, honey, garlic, and chili paste in a medium saucepan. Cook and stir over medium heat until peanut butter melts and sauce is heated through.
Add drained noodles to peanut butter sauce; toss to coat. Garnish with green onions and peanuts.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter Noodles
raw_recipe.description: Chinese peanut butter noodles are coated in a sweet and salty sauce made with peanut butter, honey, soy sauce, and ginger simmered with chicken broth.

review.reviewBody: I love this recipe. One of my favorite dishes is cold sesame noodles. This recipe might be made with peanut butter, but it's the best home version I've found. Because I've been living abroad for the past several years, I've had to learn to recreate such culinary memories at home - and this particular dish was the hardest to get just right. I've spent the last two months making this sauce at least three or four times a week, using recipes from all over the internet - including those of celebrity chefs (and if you're interested, Tyler Florence's recipe for sesame noodles is also really worth trying). But for ease of preparation and great taste, this recipe is just my favorite. If you want to play around with it, you can try adding sesame oil or a little vinegar to cut the sweetness - but I think it's best as it is. Scallions cut on the bias, julienned cucumbers, julienned carrots, chopped peanuts, or toasted sesame seeds all make fantastic additions. This is also a perfect sauce for cracked pepper grilled chicken. This sauce is savory, sweet, spicy, smooth, sticky, kid friendly, fast, cheap, and delicious. Try it!

I’ve been making this for my family for years because my kids love it and I almost always have the ingredients on hand. I reduce the ginger significantly (because I just don’t love it) and add a little sesame oil. Sometimes I use chunky peanut butter and leave out the extra peanuts on top. I’ll often add chicken, edamame, carrots or whatever I’ve got to add some color and nutrition. As it sits, it can get dry and gluey, so you should reserve some pasta water to keep it creamy.

I couldn't believe how good this was! My husband had a fantastic Thai peanut butter noodle dish at one of our fave restaurants and couldn't stop raving about it, so I decided to try to recreate it. As I can't have peanuts, I used almond butter in place of the peanut butter, and my husband said he couldn't even tell the difference! Other than the almond butter, I kept the sauce EXACTLY the same. To make the dish itself more like the restaurant version, I first stir-fried 1 lb. sliced chicken breast with some snow peas, water chesnuts, julienned carrots and red bell pepper, and even with all that thrown in, there was still plenty of sauce to coat everything completely. When I make it again, the only change I will make is to omit the additional nuts. I added toasted almonds in place of the peanuts, and they didn't stand out enough to make the extra calories worth it. By the way, with the veggies and the chicken, this made 4 verrrrrry large portions, and with far fewer calories than you would expect from a nut-butter-based dish (500). AWESOME RECIPE--Thank you so much!!

This is a great meal over all. but their is way to much ginger in it.
I think the next time I make this meal I will grate the ginger instead of mincing it, and I would cut it back to a half tbsp.

A recipe is a guide. Make it the first time as is; then make it to your taste. I used 2 Tbs peanut butter, both red pepper flakes and chili paste cilantro and julienned cucumber garnish, and toasted sesame seeds.

Enjoyed very much. The chili paste is listed as optional, but I think it would have been too sweet without it. I also started with half the recommended amount (of chili paste), then had to double the rest of the recipe as it was HOT to my taste. I've also added ~1/4 tea. of sesame oil at times. This lists as a kid friendly recipe...perhaps WITHOUT the chili paste. Final note: I've doubled this with a bit of flour to thicken for a great sauce for vegetables (kid friendly with cautious use of the chili!). It does okay without soy for those allergic (step up the sesame oil and add a sprinkle of sesame seeds if you wish.) Thanks for the recipe!

Okay, I RARELY submit reviews of any kind, but these noodles are SERIOUSLY out of this world! I was on the fence about trying the recipe, since I've tried several Asian-inspired recipes using peanut butter and have been disappointed each time. This recipe gets it right on the money. 

I served the noodles to my husband and kiddos, ages 5 and 2, and everyone went wild over them. NOTE: I used organic peanut butter, which I think made a HUGE difference in the taste of the sauce. Natural peanut butter would give the same flavor/consistency as organic. I think anything like Jiff would overpower the flavor of the sauce with a heavier peanut butter/sugary flavor. I also held off on the chili paste and chose to use Sriracha Chili Sauce on my husband's and my plates after making the noodles. 

I set up everone's plate so they could add their own toppings. In addition to the peanuts and green onions I chose to include some edamame, shredded carrot, seasoned diced chicken, and a lime wedge. The kiddos loved being able to "make their own" noodles, and I love that it was all healthy choices and delicious at the same time. 

If I could give this recipe 10 stars, I would...can't wait to make it again!

really creamy and really delicious!
i used natural peanut butter (the one with the oil on top) and found that the overall recipe wasn't sweet enough so i had to up the honey about 2x. also, i used rice noodles instead of udon (wheat allergy), and added a touch of coconut milk and toasted sesame oil, julienned carrots, bean sprouts, and shrimp on top of everything else the recipe called for. also, i like it extra spicy so i added about 2x the amount of sriracha. when i was cooking the sauce before adding it to the noodles it looked a bit too runny, but do not worry--the sauce will thicken up over time once you add it to the noodles.

Great recipe! I gave it four stars because I didn't have green onions or peanuts and I augmented the recipe a bit. I used Sriracha instead of chili paste (1 tsp to start; season with more if you like it hot). I also put it in the fridge after it cooled to room temperature. I garnished it with shredded carrot and cucumber (seeded then chopped).

I used spaghetti noodles as suggested - no issues at all. I sustituted a few pinches of red pepper flake for the chili paste and added shredded carrots to the toppings, and served with steamed broccoli to mix in. 
Also, the sauce was quite thick and on the verge of scorching in the pan, so I added about a tablespoon of sesame oil. This improved the consistency and kept the sugars from burning.
It was delicious! The fresh green onion was a perfect counter to the creamy rich sauce. I would love to try a little cilantro for an additional garnish.
Followed the instructions and it was more of a soup than sauce. Reduced it for 30 minutes on low and that did the trick. It was delicious!
Made as listed. Was a nice change for a side dish.

Ginger gives it a tiny bit of a bite, but that's okay. I don't feel this is something I'd make as a "main" in future, but it would make a decent "side". I DO love peanut butter, so that certainly isn't the problem. But my wife and I thought it was just okay.
Would use one small clove garlic to start. Also add a bit of shredded carrot, maybe red pepper and shredded chicken. Don't think kids would go for it.
We topped with thin sliced beef for a complete meal and steamed dumplings on the side.
I loved it cause the texture was very good like it was creamy and just delicious!
No changes. Too gingery for me.
Excellent sauce! It renders a very small amount. That's why I doubled the quantities and also added sautéed vegetables: onion, pepper, bak choy, shiitake mushrooms, kohlrabi and added - yummy yummy

Made this for a dinner when my grand niece and nephew were visiting. It is soooooo good! They loved it as did everyone at the table. I doubled the recipe and added a splash of sesame oil and a splash of hot chili oil. Also used thin spaghetti noodles. Delicious!!! And easy peasy. Gonna be my go to dish for any picnics or parties coming up!
